oval.etymology: F. ovale, fr. L. ovum egg. Cf. Egg, Ovum.

roots.meaning: A suffix used in medical terms to denote an inflammatory disease of; as, arthritis; bronchitis, phrenitis.

ovary.etymology: NL. ovarium, fr. L. ovum egg: cf. F. ovaire. See Oval.

ovate.etymology: L. ovatus, from ovum egg. See Oval.

ovation.etymology: L. ovatio, fr. ovare to exult, rejoice, triumph in an ovation; cf. Gr. ovation.

oven.etymology: AS. ofen; akin to D. oven, OHG. ofan, ovan, G. ofen, Icel. ofn, Dan. ovn, Sw. ugn, Goth. aúhns, Gr. ukha pot.

over.etymology: AS. ofer; akin to D. over, G. über, OHG. ubir, ubar, Dan. over, Sw. öfver, Icel. yfir, Goth. ufar, L. super, Gr. upari. Above, Eaves, Hyper-, Orlop, Super-, Sovereign, Up.

roots.meaning: A prefix equivalent to super- or per-; as hyperoxide, or peroxide. [Obs.] See Per-.

A prefix formerly much used to denote that the ingredient to the name of which it was prefixed was present in a large, or unusually large, proportion as compared with the other ingredients; as in calcium superphosphate. It has been superseded by per-, bi-, di-, acid, etc. (as peroxide, bicarbonate, disulphide, and acid sulphate), which retain the old meanings of super-, but with sharper definition. Cf. Acid, a., Bi-, Di-, and Per-.

overcome.etymology: AS. ofercuman. See Over, Come, and cf. Supervene.

overflow.etymology: AS. oferfl. See Over, and Flow.

overleap.etymology: AS. oferhleápan. See Over, and Leap.

overplus.etymology: Over + L. plus more. See Plus, and cf. Surplus.

oversee.etymology: AS. oferséon to survey, to despise. See Over, and See.

overt.etymology: OF. overt, F. ouvert, p. p. of OF. ovrir, F. ouvrir, to open, of uncertain origin; cf. It. aprire, OIt. also oprire, L. aperire to open, operire to cover, deoperire to uncover. Perch. from L. aperire influenced by F. couvrir to cover. Cf. Aperient, Cover.

overtone.etymology: A translation of G. oberton. See Over,Tone.

overture.etymology: OF. overture, F. ouverture, fr. OF. ovrir, F. ouvrir. See Overt.

ovine.etymology: L. ovinus, fr. ovis sheep: cf. F. ovine.

oviparous.etymology: L. oviparus; ovum egg + parere to bring forth: cf. F. ovipare.

ovipositor.etymology: L. ovum an egg + positor a placer, fr. ponere to place.

roots.meaning: A suffix or combining form meaning like, resembling, in the form of; as in anthropoid, asteroid, spheroid.

ovolo.etymology: It. ovolo, uovolo, fr. L. ovum an egg. Cf. Ovule.

ovule.etymology: Dim. of L. ovum an egg: cf. F. ovule. Cf. Ovolo, Ovulum.

owe.etymology: OE. owen, awen,aghen, to have, own, have (to do), hence, owe, AS. agan to have; akin to G. eigen, a., own, Icel. eiga to have, Dan. eie, Sw. äga, Goth. áigan, Skr. Ought, v., 2d Own, Fraught.

owing.etymology: Used in a passive sense for owed (AS. agen. See Own).

owl.etymology: AS. ; akin to D. uil, OHG. , G. eule, Icel. ugla, Sw. ugla, Dan. ugle.

own.etymology: OE. unnen to grant, permit, be pleased with, AS. unnan to grant; akin to OS. giunnan, G. gönnen, Icel. unna; of uncertain origin. This word has been confused with own to possess.

oxide.etymology: F. oxygène oxigen + acide acid: cf. F. oxyde. The French word was correctly spelt oxide, till about the year 1840, when, in ignorance or forgetfulness of the true history and composition of the word, the orthography was change to make it represent the u of Gr. 'oxy`s, from which it was supposed to be directly derived.

oxlip.etymology: AS. oxanslyppe. See Ox, and Cowslip.

roots.meaning: A prefix, also used adjectively, designating: (a) A compound containing oxygen. (b) A compound containing the hydroxyl group, more properly designated by hydroxy-. See Hydroxy-. Oxy acid. See Oxyacid (below).
